Value iteration

Policy iteration waits for each evaluation to finish before improving. Value iteration doesn't wait: every sweep backs up each state with the best action instead of the policy's action. One button does both jobs.

The bridge from Lesson 32: goal $+10$, water $-10$, $\gamma = 0.9$. The arrows are greedy with respect to the current values. Amber arrows are not yet optimal. Click a cell to see its backup.

The maths

Value iteration turns the Bellman optimality equation (Lesson 29) into an update, the way Lesson 30 did with the expectation equation:

$$v_{k+1}(s) = \max_a \sum_{s', r} p(s', r \mid s, a)\,\big[r + \gamma\, v_k(s')\big]$$

Compare with policy evaluation: the weighted average over $\pi(a \mid s)$ has become a max over $a$. Equivalently, it is policy iteration where each evaluation is cut down to a single sweep, using the greedy action.

Convergence. Two maxima can differ by no more than the largest gap between their terms: $|\max_a f(a) - \max_a g(a)| \le \max_a |f(a) - g(a)|$. Apply that with $v_*$, which satisfies the same equation:

$$\begin{aligned} |v_{k+1}(s) - v_*(s)| &\le \max_a \gamma \sum_{s', r} p(s', r \mid s, a)\,|v_k(s') - v_*(s')| \\ &\le \gamma \max_{s'} |v_k(s') - v_*(s')| \end{aligned}$$

The worst error shrinks by a factor $\gamma$ per sweep, the same rate as Lesson 30.

When to stop. Write $\|x\| = \max_s |x(s)|$. By the triangle inequality and the line above,

$$\|v_{k+1} - v_*\| \le \gamma\|v_k - v_{k+1}\| + \gamma\|v_{k+1} - v_*\| \;\Rightarrow\; \|v_{k+1} - v_*\| \le \frac{\gamma}{1-\gamma}\,\Delta$$

where $\Delta = \|v_{k+1} - v_k\|$ is the largest change in the last sweep. So a small $\Delta$ certifies small error, and the loop stops when $\Delta$ falls below a threshold. At the end, act greedily with respect to the final values.
